title: Incense
hookLine: let my prayer rise like incense (Psalm 141:2)

cards: The smell arrives first. Sweet and sharp, resin and wood smoke, reaching the back of the church before the procession does. Then the sound: a small chain clinking.
A priest comes up the aisle swinging a metal censer, and with every swing a gray ribbon of smoke curls out, hangs in the light from a high window, and slowly climbs.

He turns and swings it toward the icons, toward the altar, and then toward the people, who bow as it passes. By the end of the service the smoke has drifted up into the roof, and the smell is in everyone's coats.

teach.h: LET MY PRAYER BE SET FORTH AS INCENSE.
teach.b: Incense is a part of worship you can watch going up, and more than one passage ties that rising smoke to prayer.
Start with the psalm: "Let my prayer be set forth before thee as incense; and the lifting up of my hands as the evening sacrifice."
The psalmist wants their prayer to do what the smoke does: rise, and be noticed. Next, the temple.

At the start of Luke's Gospel, a priest named Zechariah is chosen by lot to go into the temple and burn incense, and Luke adds a detail: "And the whole multitude of the people were praying without at the time of incense."
Inside, smoke. Outside, prayer. The same hour, as if they were one act.

When the wise men find the child Jesus, they open their treasures: "gold, and frankincense, and myrrh." Frankincense is incense, brought by travelers from the east to be given away. Last, heaven itself.

teach.h: WITH THE PRAYERS OF THE SAINTS.
teach.b: In Revelation, an angel stands at the altar with a golden censer, "And the smoke of the incense, which came with the prayers of the saints, ascended up before God out of the angel's hand."
In that picture, the prayers rise all the way to God. Orthodox and Catholic Christians use incense in worship, and so do some Anglican and Lutheran churches.
Other Christians pray without it, and keep the psalm's thought without the smoke. In the psalm's picture, a prayer isn't meant to stay on the ground.

how: In Orthodox and Catholic worship, and in some Anglican and Lutheran churches, a priest or deacon swings a censer toward the altar, the icons or the gospel book, and the people; other churches pray without incense.

games.q: you're Zechariah, chosen by lot to burn incense in the temple. while the smoke rises inside, what are the people outside doing?
o: praying, at the same hour as the incense
games.why: "the whole multitude of the people were praying without at the time of incense." smoke inside, prayer outside, as one act.

practice: If you have incense and it's safe to light, light it and watch the smoke climb; if not, open a jar from the kitchen, cinnamon, cloves, a bay leaf, and breathe it in slowly.
Let the scent fill one breath, then another, and picture your breath rising. If you pray, you can say the psalm, let my prayer be set forth before thee as incense, or simply follow the scent.
